label: D1 drops after unrewarded S1, rises after rewarded S2; D2 tracks rare transition direction.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * prev_reward * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action - state)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 45: timing dominates (high at D1, near 0 at GO, mid at D2; R^2 0.90). Beyond timing: at D1 it is lowered when the previous trial reached S1 unrewarded (weight -0.18) and raised when it reached S2 rewarded (+0.10); a1->S2 rewarded is highest, a2->S1 unrewarded lowest, and repeated unrewarded trials push it lower further (trial-before reward adds a little). At D2 it follows the just-made transition: a2->S1 (rare) raises it, a1->S2 (rare) lowers it, common transitions are in between (term action - state). GO carries almost nothing. The free fit adds full last-trial tables at D1 and D2 (D2 is also higher after a previous a2 choice and lower after a1 S1 r), the trial-before reward and belief_lo; belief itself adds little once choice x state is in. Main-effect versions (reward + state additive) score much worse than the S1-unrewarded interaction. All terms observed; no model outputs or future variables.

issues: The label's 'D2 tracks rare transition direction' doesn't give the sign. From the residuals, rare a2->S1 is +0.157, rare a1->S2 is -0.149, and the common transitions sit between (-0.05 and +0.03), with fitted weight +0.153 on action - state. The label should say which rare transition raises the gate and which lowers it.

The claims check out on test. Reward and state as separate D1 main effects score 0.40, against 0.61 for the recorded form, so the S1-unrewarded interaction matters (the explanation said about 0.35). Turning the D2 term into a single a2->S1 indicator drops the score to 0.50. Replacing the D1 S2-rewarded term with S2 alone gives 0.57. The ordering 'a1 S2 r highest, a2 S1 u lowest' matches the residual table (+0.16 / -0.20).
The claim that runs of unrewarded trials push the gate down is only weakly supported: reward two trials back gets a weight of +0.026 at D1.

Moderate systematic errors from the previous choice remain, and the label leaves them out. At D1, a previous a1 is under-predicted (a1 S2 u +0.066, a1 S2 r +0.065) and a previous a2 over-predicted (a2 S1 r -0.059). At D2, a previous a2 is under-predicted (a2 S2 u +0.060) and a1 S1 r over-predicted (-0.078). These errors are about 0.06-0.08, against term effects of 0.10-0.18.

At D2 the residual also falls steadily with belief (decile 0 at +0.08, decile 9 at -0.09). Adding belief_lo or prev_action to the short form did not beat it: 0.58 and 0.43. The best alternative I found, with the D1 terms rewritten as prev_reward - (prev_state == S1) plus the S1-unrewarded term, scores 0.616 against 0.612, which is not a meaningful gain.
The short form reaches 0.61 on test, against an observed-only ceiling of 0.81 and a free fit of 0.76. None of its terms looks like curve fitting.
skeptic.revised_label: D1: low after unrewarded S1, high after rewarded S2; D2: raised by rare a2->S1, lowered by rare a1->S2.

final_label: D1: low after unrewarded S1, high after rewarded S2; D2: raised by rare a2->S1, lowered by rare a1->S2.
